extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to BMC Psychology (researchers and academics)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, formatting, and submitting manuscripts (research articles and other article types) to the open-access journal BMC Psychology, including editorial policies, peer review expectations, data and file requirements, and licensing/APC information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims and scope / journal suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you submit to the most suitable journal; BMC Psychology welcomes a broad range of topics in psychology (developmental, clinical, cognitive, experimental, theoretical, health, social, policy/law, personality, psychobiology, human-technology interaction, sports/exercise, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check the journal scope before submission. As a BMC Series journal, editorial decisions are not made on perceived interest or impact; manuscripts are considered if scientifically valid. Use the topic list to judge fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific validity (research articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research articles are considered for publication if they are scientifically valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research articles this includes having a clearly defined and sound research question, appropriate methodology and analysis, and adherence to community-agreed standards relevant to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript submission eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript can only be submitted by an author of the manuscript and may not be submitted by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only authors may submit. Ensure the submitting person is one of the authors to avoid administrative rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: General manuscript formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting rules for article types and general formatting guidance for the main manuscript text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick points: use double-line spacing; include line and page numbering; use SI units; ensure special characters are embedded in the text; do not use page breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable file formats and editable files requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted main manuscript file formats and requirement that files be editable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable formats: Microsoft Word (DOC, DOCX), Rich Text Format (RTF), TeX/LaTeX. Editable files are required for production. If non-editable files (e.g., PDFs) are submitted, authors will be required to re-submit editable versions during revision or after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: TeX/LaTeX submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for TeX/LaTeX users preparing submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template. A PDF will be compiled during submission using pdfLaTeX and TexLive 2021. All relevant editable source files must be uploaded; failing to submit source files will delay production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation to provide datasets and materials that support the manuscript conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should deposit datasets in publicly available repositories where appropriate, or present them in the main paper or additional supporting files. Provide datasets in machine-readable formats (spreadsheets rather than PDFs). Where community expectations exist for repository archiving, deposition is mandatory. Include an 'Availability of data and materials' section using the prescribed wording and include unique identifiers/DOIs for datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Required wording/formats for the 'Availability of data and materials' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data are in a repository: "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) available in the [repository name] repository, [unique persistent identifier and hyperlink to dataset(s) in https:// format]." If data are included as additional files: "The dataset(s) supporting the conclusions of this article is(are) included within the article (and its additional file(s))." Publicly available datasets must be fully referenced in the reference list with an accession number or DOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Database and software metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Information required when submitting databases or software as part of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Databases: state the web/ftp address and restrictions to use by non-academics. Software: include project name, project home page, archived version DOI or unique identifier, operating system(s), programming language, other requirements, license (e.g., GNU GPL), and any restrictions to use by non-academics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: What can and cannot be included in the reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only articles, clinical trial registration records and abstracts that have been published or are in press, or are available through public e-print/preprint servers, may be cited in the reference list. Unpublished abstracts, unpublished data and personal communications should not be included in the reference list but may be mentioned in-text as "unpublished observations" or "personal communications" (with permission). Journal abbreviations should follow Index Medicus/MEDLINE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting and web links
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format references and handle web links/URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Instructions for Authors for the relevant article type for the reference style. All web links and URLs (including authors' own websites) should be given a reference number and included in the reference list rather than within the text. Provide full details including site title, URL, and date accessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering, order and composite files
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for figure ordering and multi-panel figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures should be numbered in the order they are first mentioned in the text and uploaded in this order. Multi-panel figures (parts a, b, c, etc.) should be submitted as a single composite file containing all parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure titles, legends and keys
rubrics_metrics.description: Length limits and placement for figure titles, legends and keys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure titles: maximum 15 words; figure legends: maximum 300 words and should be provided in the main manuscript (not in the graphic file). Figure keys should be incorporated into the graphic itself, not placed into the legend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure cropping, size, resolution and technical specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: How figures should be prepared so information is legible and suitable for web and PDF publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crop figures to minimise white space. Web figure widths: 600 pixels (standard) and 1200 pixels (high resolution). Final PDF widths: 85 mm (half page) and 170 mm (full page); maximum height 225 mm. Image resolution: approximately 300 dpi at final size. All lines should be wider than 0.25 pt at standard widths. All fonts must be embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file types and compression guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted file types for figures and recommendations to minimise quality loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted formats: EPS, PDF, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, TIFF, JPEG, PNG, BMP, CDX (ChemDraw). Vector figures should be submitted as PDF where possible. TIFF files should be saved with LZW (lossless) compression. JPEG files should be saved at maximum quality. Minimise conversions between file types to avoid degradation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission for previously published figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility and how to indicate permissions for reused material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must obtain permission from the copyright holder to reproduce figures or tables previously published elsewhere. Permission should be indicated in the figure legend and the original source must be included in the reference list. For open access compatibility, permission is required if previously published in non-open access journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering, placement and large tables handling
rubrics_metrics.description: How to number, place and provide large tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables should be numbered and cited in sequence (Table 1, Table 2, etc.). Tables smaller than one A4/Letter page can be placed within the manuscript at the appropriate location. Tables larger than one page should be placed at the end of the document with a citation where they should appear. Very large/wide tables can be uploaded as additional files (Excel or CSV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table titles, legends and formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Title/legend length and permitted formatting within tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table titles: maximum 15 words and included above the table. Table legends: maximum 300 words and included underneath the table. Tables should be formatted using the 'Table object' function (not embedded as figures or spreadsheet images). Color and shading may not be used. Highlighting may use superscript, numbering, lettering, symbols or bold text with explanations in the legend. Do not use commas to indicate numerical values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional files: inclusion, naming, metadata and size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for supplementary/additional files provided with a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can provide datasets, tables, movies, or other supporting information as additional files. All additional files will be published with the accepted article. Do not include patient consent forms, certificates of language editing, or revised main manuscripts with tracked changes (send by email if requested). Maximum file size for additional files is 20 MB each; files will be virus-scanned. Each additional file should be named 'Additional file 1' etc. and cited explicitly in the manuscript. Provide file name, file format/extension, title of data, and description in a separate section of the manuscript text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that should be included in the cover letter at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explanation of why the manuscript should be published in BMC Psychology; an explanation of any issues relating to journal policies; a declaration of any potential competing interests; confirmation that all authors have approved the manuscript for submission; confirmation that content has not been published or submitted elsewhere. If submitting to a special issue, name the issue in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting potential peer reviewers and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: How authors may suggest reviewers and list exclusions in the cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may suggest potential peer reviewers and should provide institutional email addresses where possible, or identifiers to help verify identity (ORCID or Scopus ID). Intentionally falsifying reviewer information will result in rejection and possible investigation under the misconduct policy. Authors may also list individuals they prefer not to review their manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review criteria and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the peer review process and the criteria reviewers use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review typically uses two or more experts who assess validity and robustness. Reviewers evaluate based primarily on three criteria: scientific robustness (methodology and whether data support conclusions), originality (does it duplicate existing work), and clarity (is the manuscript clear and coherent). Editors make decisions based on reviewers' reports and may consult the editorial board. BMC Psychology operates transparent peer review: if published, reviewer reports are published alongside the article under a Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0, but reviewers are not named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of competing interests by reviewers and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for reviewers and editors to declare competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and editors are required to declare competing interests and can be excluded from the peer review process if a competing interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer options and author control
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and author rights when transferring a manuscript to another journal within the publisher's portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a manuscript is not accepted, authors may be offered a transfer to another Springer Nature journal. Transfer offers provide choice, save time (no reformatting necessary), and can move files and reviewer comments. Transfers are not automatic — the author must agree to and complete the transfer. Authors may decline and withdraw a transfer at any point by contacting the Transfer Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and optional editing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that manuscripts be presented in well-written English and optional support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting work in good English helps editors/reviewers assess it fairly. Authors may use colleagues or professional language editing services (Springer Nature Author Services, AJE language checker). Use of these services is not required and does not guarantee selection for review or acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article processing charge (APC), waivers and discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access APC applies to accepted articles and waiver/discount availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A current APC applies (stated in currency values on the page) and is subject to VAT/local taxes. Springer Nature offers institutional agreements, funder/institutional support, and discretionary waivers/discounts (especially for corresponding authors in lowest-income countries). Requests for APC waivers/discounts must be made at the point of submission; requests during review or after acceptance cannot be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access licensing options and author copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing options (CC BY-NC-ND or CC BY) and that authors retain copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMC Psychology articles are published under Creative Commons licences: CC BY-NC-ND or CC BY. Under Creative Commons licences authors retain copyright. CC BY-NC-ND allows sharing for non-commercial purposes with credit, and requires permission for commercial reuse or derivatives. CC BY allows sharing and adaptation for any purpose (including commercial) with credit. Authors may need to select licence variations to meet funder/institutional requirements.
